newsitem.title: FRANCE: WPP seeks to boost business in France - Le Monde.
newsitem.headline: WPP seeks to boost business in France - Le Monde.

text.p: WPP Group Plc, the world's largest advertising and marketing services group, is seeking to boost its market share in France, chairman Martin Sorrell said in an interview published on Tuesday in Le Monde newspaper.
"In France we want to increase our market share in public relations and design. We also want to continue to develop J. Walter Thompson", he said.
Sorrell said it was possible WPP would merge the media-buying operations of units J. Walter Thompson and Ogilvy & Mather.

"What we need to do for our clients is to increase our purchasing power to be able to negotiate, but without antagonism, and to develop media techniques like sponsoring and co-producing television programmes," he said.
"That is why J. Walter Thompson and Ogilvy & Mather should buy advertising space together, he said.
Sorrell said WPP would continue to grow both organically and through acquisitions.
He said he was still interested in BDDP, the French advertising agency that was bought last year by Britain's GGT.
"I am interested. But it difficult to put this interest into practice," he said. DT/SLA/KEC
